title: S3-Tracker: Self-Supervised Surgical Tissue Tracking With Contrastive Random Walks
summary: Robust point tracking in endoscopic videos is essential for computer-assisted intervention and autonomous robotic surgery, enabling continuous registration between intraoperative video and preoperative imaging despite soft tissue deformation. However, supervised tracking methods depend on large annotated datasets, while surgical conditions make reliable trajectory annotation challenging. We propose a self-supervised Track-Any-Point approach that learns from unlabeled surgical videos by establishing global pixel correspondences and inferring point trajectories through contrastive random walks. Trained without annotations, our method achieves performance comparable to existing semi-supervised approaches while implicitly handling tissue deformation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of self-supervised point tracking in surgical environments and its potential to reduce reliance on annotated data.
tldr: This paper introduces S3-Tracker, a self-supervised Track-Any-Point method for endoscopic surgical videos that learns global pixel correspondences and infers tissue trajectories via contrastive random walks, avoiding the need for annotated trajectory data while achieving performance comparable to semi-supervised approaches.
tldr_zh: 本文提出S3-Tracker，一种用于内窥镜手术视频的自监督点追踪方法，通过对比随机游走建立全局像素对应并推断组织运动轨迹，无需标注数据即可达到与半监督方法相当的性能。
summary_zh:
摘要：
内窥镜视频中的鲁棒点跟踪对于计算机辅助介入和自主机器人手术至关重要，能够在软组织变形的情况下实现术中视频与术前影像之间的连续配准。然而，有监督跟踪方法依赖于大量标注数据集，而手术条件使得可靠的轨迹标注具有挑战性。我们提出了一种自监督的Track-Any-Point方法，通过建立全局像素对应关系并利用对比随机游走推断点轨迹，从未标注的手术视频中学习。该方法无需标注即可训练，在隐式处理组织变形的同时，达到了与现有半监督方法相当的性能。这些研究结果证明了自监督点跟踪在手术环境中的可行性，及其在减少对标注数据依赖方面的潜力。

title: Fusing Spectral Signatures and Activation Clustering for Backdoor Detection in Healthcare Imaging Models: Method, Implementation, and Evaluation
summary: Machine learning models are increasingly deployed in healthcare imaging pipelines for diagnostic support, and training-time attacks against them are a named sector-level concern: healthcare-sector guidance identifies model poisoning and adversarial attacks as threats requiring dedicated defenses, while federal policy directs expanded AI vulnerability-detection tooling to critical infrastructure operators such as rural hospitals. Spectral signature analysis and activation clustering are two established backdoor detection methods routinely evaluated as independent baselines, but their outputs are not ordinarily combined, and reported detection performance on medical imaging benchmarks remains sparse relative to the natural-image setting. This paper contributes three things: a score-level fusion rule combining per-class spectral ranking with activation-clustering flags into a single per-sample poisoning score and a model-level agreement statistic; an open-source implementation of the resulting eight-stage pipeline; and an evaluation of that pipeline against synthetically poisoned variants of a public medical imaging benchmark and CIFAR-10 at four poisoning rates (0%, 1%, 5%, 10%) over five seeds each, measuring each detector alone against the fusion. On the medical benchmark, the fused detector reaches AUROC >= 0.99 at every nonzero poisoning rate tested. On CIFAR-10, fusion does not uniformly help: at 10% poisoning, activation clustering's true-positive rate collapses to 0.000 and spectral AUROC independently degrades to near-chance (0.545), despite a 97.2% attack success rate confirming the backdoor was fully installed. The fused score, a weighted combination of both signals, inherits this joint failure. Detection output is expressed in NIST AI RMF Measure-function and MITRE ATLAS terms, so findings are reported in the vocabulary security and compliance teams already use.
tldr: This paper proposes a fusion of spectral signature analysis and activation clustering for detecting backdoor attacks in healthcare imaging models, achieving high AUROC on medical benchmarks but revealing failure modes on CIFAR-10. The method is implemented as an open-source pipeline and evaluated on synthetically poisoned datasets.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种融合光谱特征分析和激活聚类的方法，用于检测医疗影像模型中的后门攻击，在医疗基准上取得了高AUROC，但在CIFAR-10上暴露了失败模式。该方法以开源流水线实现，并在合成中毒数据集上进行了评估。
summary_zh: 机器学习模型正越来越多地被部署于医疗影像管线中以提供诊断支持，而针对这些模型的训练时攻击已被列为特定行业层面的关注点：医疗行业指南将模型投毒和对抗攻击列为需要专门防御的威胁，联邦政策则指示将扩展的AI漏洞检测工具应用于农村医院等关键基础设施运营商。频谱特征分析和激活聚类是两种已确立的后门检测方法，通常作为独立基线进行评估，但它们的输出通常不进行组合，且相对于自然图像场景，在医学影像基准上的检测性能报告仍然较少。本文贡献了三点：一种分数级融合规则，将每类频谱排名与激活聚类标记相结合，生成单样本投毒分数和模型级一致性统计量；所得到的八阶段管线的开源实现；以及该管线在合成投毒变体的公共医学影像基准和CIFAR-10上的评估，涉及四个投毒率（0%、1%、5%、10%），每个投毒率各采用五个种子，分别测量单个检测器与融合检测器的性能。在医学基准上，融合检测器在测试的每个非零投毒率下均达到AUROC >= 0.99。在CIFAR-10上，融合并非始终有益：在10%投毒率下，激活聚类的真阳性率降至0.000，频谱AUROC独立退化至接近随机水平（0.545），尽管97.2%的攻击成功率证实后门已完全植入。融合分数作为两种信号的加权组合，继承了这一共同失效。检测输出以NIST AI RMF测量功能和MITRE ATLAS术语表述，因此研究结果采用安全与合规团队已使用的词汇报告。
